I farm here in Oromia with my family, and this small sorghum plot near the house is one I know well. I have some schooling but money is tight, so I only buy a little DAP and urea when I can — sorghum does not need as much as maize, and the rains here usually carry it. I keep some manure from our cattle for this plot since it is close to the compound, and I save my own seed from last year because the improved sorghum seed is expensive and not always available at the cooperative. We depend on the rain, not irrigation, and my wife and older children help me with weeding and bird-scaring when the heads start to fill.
